rules.basis: The NP sheet's table prints 'Output Power' in watts, 1000 for the 12NP10, and the lines carry no unit in the reading, so this sheet's figures are read in watts.
The 12LP10 sheet's heading says 'Watts Cont.' and the line prints a bare 1000, so it is read in watts.

The MM, CSW and other inverter sheets print one 'Output Power' beside the surge and idle figures, 400 W for the 12-400N; a line printed without a unit on a sheet this file does not name stays a gap rather than being read in watts.

The MM-AE sheet prints its 'Power consumption' lines, search mode and no load, as bare figures, 6 and 18 for the MM1512AE, where the MS sheets print the same lines as watts; this sheet's figures are read in watts.

The MS and MM sheets print the inverter's draw under 'Power consumption' as 'Search mode' and 'No load (120 VAC output, typical)'; the search-mode figure carries its mode in its name. The MMS912E prints its search draw in amps under the same name, '0.4 ADC at 12.6 V', which reads as a gap that says so.
The MSH and MS-PAE sheets state the no-load draw while inverting; the word is 'inverting', which the reader does not take as a mode, so the rule states it.
The same sheets state the draw while searching for a load, which is the search mode.

The NP inverter sheets print 'AC Voltage' and the CSW sheets 'AC Output Voltage @ 12.5V' for the 120 V output; the bare 'Output Voltage' is not read, since the ADI charger sheets, whose models are filed as inverters, print their 27.6 V DC output under it. A tolerance printed with the figure is refused rather than halved.
The battery sheets state their own nominal voltage, 12 V; the CSW sheets' 'DC Input Voltage (Nominal)' of 12.5 V is the input the ratings are taken at, not a bank voltage, and is not read.

The charger section of the MS, MM and RD sheets states the continuous output in amps DC at 25 °C: 105 A for the MS4024PAE, 110 A for the RD2212, 50 A for the MM1012E, whose line carries no unit in the reading and is read in amps; the inverter's continuous figure on the same sheets is in VA under 'Continuous power output'.

The MM and RD sheets state surge power for 5 s, 30 s, 5 min and 30 min, each on its own line with the time in its name, which is the duration the key needs; most lines carry no unit in the reading and are gaps until they do.
The MS-PAE sheets state the same four surge figures under headings that say 'real watts', so a line printed without a unit is read in watts.
